content.title:
Scored quiz
Module 4
content.intro: This quiz covers all the lessons in this module. You must achieve 80% to pass. Good luck!

questions.prompt: What should an example question look like?

options.value: It should look like this option.
I think this option would be best.

correct.title: Correct
correct.body: Option 1 and Option 2 are the best choices for certain specific reasons.

wrong.title: Incorrect
wrong.body: Option 1 and Option 2 are the best choices for certain specific reasons.

questions.prompt: What are the three key factors ESG stands for in sustainable energy finance?

correct.title: Correct
correct.body: ESG refers to Environmental, Social, and Governance factors, which are used to guide sustainable investments and assess their broader impacts.

wrong.title: Incorrect
wrong.body: ESG refers to Environmental, Social, and Governance factors, which are used to guide sustainable investments and assess their broader impacts.

questions.prompt: Which of the following are advantages of sustainable finance? (Select all that apply)

correct.title: Correct
correct.body: Sustainable finance enhances corporate responsibility, creates long-term value, and manages risk by integrating ESG factors into decision-making.

wrong.title: Incorrect
wrong.body: Sustainable finance enhances corporate responsibility, creates long-term value, and manages risk by integrating ESG factors into decision-making.

questions.prompt: Which region received only 2% of global clean energy investment between 2000 and 2024?

correct.title: Correct
correct.body: Sub-Saharan Africa received just 2% of global clean energy investments, despite having significant unmet energy needs.

wrong.title: Incorrect
wrong.body: Sub-Saharan Africa received just 2% of global clean energy investments, despite having significant unmet energy needs.

questions.prompt: What is the estimated annual clean energy investment needed in EMDEs (Emerging Markets and Developing Economies) by the early 2030s?

correct.title: Correct
correct.body: EMDEs need between $2.2 and $2.8 trillion annually to meet clean energy investment requirements by the early 2030s.

wrong.title: Incorrect
wrong.body: EMDEs need between $2.2 and $2.8 trillion annually to meet clean energy investment requirements by the early 2030s.

questions.prompt: Which instruments are commonly used in blended finance? (Select all that apply)

correct.title: Correct
correct.body: Blended finance uses tools such as subordinated debt, guarantees, and technical assistance grants to de-risk investments.

wrong.title: Incorrect
wrong.body: Blended finance uses tools such as subordinated debt, guarantees, and technical assistance grants to de-risk investments.

options.value: A project supported by a commercial bank
A project guaranteed by the government
A project that can reliably generate revenue to repay loans
A project funded only through public financing

correct.title: Correct
correct.body: A bankable project is financially viable, able to generate consistent revenue, and low-risk, making it attractive to investors.

wrong.title: Incorrect
wrong.body: A bankable project is financially viable, able to generate consistent revenue, and low-risk, making it attractive to investors.

questions.prompt: Which of the following are considered barriers to clean energy investment in EMDEs? (Select all that apply)

correct.title: Correct
correct.body: Common barriers in EMDEs include unclear regulations, high capital costs, and outdated or limited infrastructure.

wrong.title: Incorrect
wrong.body: Common barriers in EMDEs include unclear regulations, high capital costs, and outdated or limited infrastructure.

questions.prompt: In 2023, how much global investment went into clean energy?

correct.title: Correct
correct.body: According to the IEA, global investment in clean energy reached $1.7 trillion in 2023.

wrong.title: Incorrect
wrong.body: According to the IEA, global investment in clean energy reached $1.7 trillion in 2023.

questions.prompt: What is the 'Triple Penalty' faced by EMDEs in energy transition?

options.value: Lack of investors, skills, and governance
Subsidy cuts, currency volatility, and migration

correct.title: Correct
correct.body: The triple penalty includes affordability challenges, fossil fuel dependence, and limited access to technologies and skills.

wrong.title: Incorrect
wrong.body: The triple penalty includes affordability challenges, fossil fuel dependence, and limited access to technologies and skills.

questions.prompt: Which policy instruments are used by the public sector to support renewable energy? (Select all that apply)

correct.title: Correct
correct.body: Supportive instruments include feed-in tariffs, carbon pricing, and energy performance contracts. Fuel subsidies generally discourage renewables.

wrong.title: Incorrect
wrong.body: Supportive instruments include feed-in tariffs, carbon pricing, and energy performance contracts. Fuel subsidies generally discourage renewables.
